transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Lila Zhou (NovaScribe - Head of ML), Daniel Reyes (NovaScribe - Platform), Priya Sharma (NovaScribe - Secops)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
NovaScribe is evaluating migration off a mix of OpenAI/Anthropic hosted endpoints plus some on-prem vLLM testing. Primary concerns: inference latency SLOs for interactive editor, cost per 1M tokens, private VPC requirement for PHI-adjacent data, and eval parity for instruction fine-tuned models. They requested a microbench and security docs.

Topics:
- current stack + pain points
- model compatibility (TGI/vLLM) and tokenization/weight parity
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- security, SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
- next steps: benchmark, pricing, follow-up call

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Okay everyone thanks for joining, um let's go ahead and get started. Quick intros?
[00:07] Lila (Head of ML): Hi I'm Lila, we run model ops at NovaScribe, been doing a lot of prompt-tuning and instruction tuning, using OpenAI for a lot of prod and trying some Anthropic for safer outputs.
[00:18] Daniel (Platform): Daniel here, platform eng, i run our infra, we're also experiment-ing with v-L-M on a couple nodes, and testing TGI stacks in k8s.
[00:29] Priya (SecOps): Priya, secops, I'm focused on data residency and audit requirements — we handle PHI-ish data for partners so need strong controls.
[00:36] Maya: Great, and i'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ethan will jump in on the technicals.
[00:41] Ethan (SE): Hey all, thanks. Quick agenda: understand current infra, perf & cost targets, what blocks migration, then talk options — hosted, dedicated, private.

[01:00] Lila: The big reason we're talking to you is parity — we have tuned a bunch of instruction checkpoints on OpenAI, and the hallucination profiles are... they vary, so we need to run eval parity across our test suite. If we can get match-or-better quality with lower cost and fast latency that's ideal.
[01:18] Maya: Can you quantify latency targets?
[01:21] Lila: Editor experience needs 200-350ms for short completions (under 256 tokens) on 95th percentile. For multi-turn summaries it's ok to be 600-800ms.
[01:33] Daniel: And cost is a hard constraint — we're targeting under $0.17 per 1k tokens effective cost today across our mix.
[01:42] Ethan: Cool. A few quick clarifying q's: are you running everything via OpenAI API now, or do you have on-prem model weights?
[01:49] Lila: Mostly API, but we have a set of fine-tuned weights for some models and we've been trying to serve them via vLLM locally — that's where the parity question comes in. TGI is in the mix too but we keep hitting memory fragmentation and slower kv-cache behavior.
[02:05] Ethan: That resonates. Our Dedicated runtime is optimized for KV cache handling and continuous batching; we often see 20-40% better throughput for causal models vs stock TGI in our workloads, depending on sequence lengths.
[02:18] Priya: On the security side, we need VPC peering, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), SSO via Okta and full audit trails. Are those supported?
[02:27] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we integrate with KMS and offer SAML SSO and token-level audit logs. We'll share docs after the call.
[02:36] Priya: Great, need to confirm encryption at rest for model artifacts too — sometimes vendors gloss over that.
[02:41] Ethan: We do offer encryption at rest for private deployments, and for Dedicated we can work with a customer-managed KMS for volume encryption. I'll include the architecture diagram.

[03:00] Daniel: One of our pain points with vLLM is the behavior differences on certain tokenizers — we had a case where stop-sequences were handled differently which broke a workflow. How do you handle tokenization parity?
[03:14] Ethan: We do tokenization normalization in our serving path, and we have model manifest metadata so you can pin tokenizer versions. For customers porting from OpenAI/Anthropic we provide a compatibility guide and quick scripts.
[03:26] Lila: For eval parity we run both automated metrics (EM, ROUGE, BLEU where relevant) and human annotations. We found that sometimes model variant selection matters more than raw FP or quant strategy.
[03:39] Maya: Are you using 4-bit quantization in prod anywhere?
[03:42] Lila: Not in prod yet. We've tried 8-bit and some QLoRA fine-tunes. Concern is quality regressions.
[03:48] Ethan: We do recommend per-workload quant profiles — e.g., keep generator models in higher precision, quantize rerankers. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant settings based on eval outcomes.

[04:05] Daniel: Can you do a proof of concept with our prompt bank? I can give you a representative 500 prompt set, including long context ones.
[04:12] Maya: Yep that's exactly what we normally do — SE will run a microbench & parity eval. Ethan, can you outline what you need?
[04:18] Ethan: I'll need the prompt set, sample payload sizes, target p95 latency, and your current token accounting method. Also whether the weights are public or need to stay inside your VPC. If weights can't leave, we can run a Private eval on your infra or run tests via a dedicated private tunnel.
[04:36] Priya: For the POC we need an NDA addendum for the model artifacts and confirmation of ephemeral logging.
[04:41] Maya: Understood, i'll attach our confidentiality addendum and a security checklist.

[05:00] Lila: One more thing — we've been considering hybrid routing: use OpenAI for a fallback when dedicated capacity is exhausted, but prefer private for PHI content. Does Redwood support routing policies?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes, policy-based routing is a core feature. You can route by model, region, and content category. We also support automatic fallback to hosted variants.
[05:21] Daniel: Oh that's good. How about autoscaling for Dedicated? We need predictable cold-start behavior and to avoid token spikes causing latency cliffs.
[05:30] Ethan: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling with warm pools for burst capacity, and you can pin minimum replicas. We also expose metrics so you can hook into your own autoscaler.
[05:40] Priya: Our compliance team will ask about data residency — EU customers must stay in eu-west for some partners. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[05:48] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported in Private and Dedicated; hosted API also supports region selection for enterprise plans. We'll include region SLA details.

[06:05] Lila: On model compatibility, if we bring our Anthropic-tuned checkpoints, any gotchas?
[06:12] Ethan: The main differences are in tokenization and RLHF reward model behavior, but the runtime can host architectures we support. We'll run a quick compatibility pass; sometimes there are optimizer state or format conversions needed.
[06:24] Lila: About costs — we want a rough estimate for a dedicated pool sized for 200 qps 95th meeting that 256 token median — see if that aligns with our $0.17 per 1k tokens.
[06:36] Maya: I'll send a back-of-envelope and a more formal quote after we get your usage traces. For the POC we can run a two-week pilot on Dedicated with discounted pilot rates.

[06:55] Daniel: Any limitations with long context models and KV caching? We've seen memory blow up in our vLLM tests beyond 8k tokens.
[07:04] Ethan: Our runtime optimizes KV eviction and supports segmented KV caching which helps long contexts; we can also suggest chunking strategies. We'll try to reproduce with your traces.

[07:20] Priya: For SSO we use Okta and SCIM; need RBAC to restrict model download. Is that doable?
[07:28] Ethan: Yes, RBAC + SCIM provisioning is in our Private offering; Dedicated can integrate with enterprise SSO as well.

[07:40] Lila: Is there an off-the-shelf eval harness? Our team wants to automate periodic parity checks so we don't regress.
[07:48] Maya: Redwood has an eval pipeline and you can plug in your test suites. It produces regression alerts and ties them to rollouts. We'll demo that in the next call if you want.

[08:05] Daniel: Let's talk timeline — we're hoping to decide in the next 6 weeks and run a pilot in Q2.
[08:12] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Next steps recap: we'll run a microbench + parity eval, send SOC2 & architecture docs, and provide pricing + Dedicated sizing.
[08:21] Priya: And we'll send the prompt bank and confirm NDA addendum.

[08:30] Maya: Anything else?
[08:33] Lila: Just one caveat — we sometimes use third-party content filters and need to keep that chain in the loop for safety.
[08:39] Ethan: No problem, we can support hooks for filtering and tool calls.

[08:50] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with notes and the links.
[08:55] Daniel: Thanks all.
[09:00] Priya: Thanks.
[09:04] Lila: bye

(End of recording)
